pages.text: **Storm Coil.** Install it on the top of a machine and put a vanilla **Lightning Rod** on it. During a thunderstorm the rod draws lightning, and every strike stores **200,000 RF** in the coil, which feeds the machine 512 RF a tick. The coil holds 400,000 RF (more on higher-tier machines); the rest of a strike is lost. It signals each strike and how full it is on two signal outputs. A Channeling trident calls lightning on demand in a storm.

**Blast Damper.** Explosions within **6 blocks** of the machine are stopped before they happen: nothing breaks and nobody is hurt, and their energy goes into the damper. A creeper gives 31,500 RF, TNT 56,000, a charged creeper 126,000. Only the nearest damper catches an explosion.

On a **Reinforced** (or better) machine the damper also detonates **TNT** from Purple storage inside the chassis, one every 5 seconds, when it has room for the energy.

**Galvanic Cell.** A battery made of two metals. The less noble one goes into **Orange storage** and is used up, one ingot every minute; the nobler one goes into **Purple storage** and stays. The **Orange tank** needs water. Power is 25 RF/t per volt of difference: iron against copper 0.78 V (20 RF/t), zinc against copper 1.10 V (28 RF/t), zinc against gold 2.26 V (57 RF/t).

Real metals use their real electrode potentials; Metallurgy's fantasy metals have invented ones (fire and shadow metals are reactive, sky and star metals noble). Pairing the rare ones is the late-game version: lutetium against etherium is close to 4.5 V.

**For pack makers.** Potentials are data: `data/<ns>/fieldframe/electrodes/*.json` with entries like `{"item": "#c:ingots/zinc", "volts": -0.76}`; KubeJS: `FieldframeEvents.electrodes(e => e.item('#c:ingots/nickel', -0.25))`. Lightning rods (`#fieldframe:lightning_rods`), explosives (`#fieldframe:explosives`) and extra electrolytes (`#fieldframe:electrolytes`) are tags.
